name: ABC
question: Does one 100 U intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA injection reduce urgency incontinence episodes differently from a six-month oral anticholinergic regimen in women with idiopathic urgency urinary incontinence?

arms.label: OnabotulinumtoxinA 100 U intradetrusor injection with oral placebo
oral solifenacin with escalation or a switch to trospium XR, plus saline injection

design.population: 249 randomized women without neurologic disease who had five or more urgency incontinence episodes per 3-day diary, were anticholinergic-naive or had used up to two anticholinergics other than solifenacin, darifenacin or trospium, and had a postvoid residual below 150 mL.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, double-placebo randomized superiority trial
design.locator: PMC3543828 Methods, Study Design; Results, Participants; Figure 1

verdictNote: Episode reduction did not differ; complete resolution favored toxin, while urinary infection and catheterization were more frequent.
takeaway: In women with idiopathic urgency urinary incontinence, one 100 U onabotulinumtoxinA injection and six months of oral solifenacin (with escalation or a switch to trospium XR) reduced daily episodes similarly (3.3 versus 3.4 fewer); toxin gave more complete resolution but more urinary infection and catheterization.

reports.label: Published protocol
reports.citation: Visco AG, Brubaker L, Richter HE, et al. "Anticholinergic versus Botulinum Toxin A Comparison Trial for the Treatment of Bothersome Urge Urinary Incontinence: ABC Trial." *Contemp Clin Trials.* 2012;33(1):184-196. doi:10.1016/j.cct.2011.09.019

delivery.label: Injection technique
delivery.value: Wolf injection cystoscope with the bladder filled with 100 to 200 mL; 10 mL containing 100 U onabotulinumtoxinA (or placebo) plus 0.1 mL indigo carmine injected at about 15 to 20 detrusor sites under direct vision with disposable needles, covering the posterior wall and dome and sparing the trigone, ureteral orifices and anterior dome, followed by a 1 mL saline flush.

delivery.label: Preinjection requirements
delivery.value: Negative dipstick urinalysis (below 1+ nitrite and below 1+ leukocyte) before injection; ineligible if postvoid residual was 150 mL or more on two occasions; patient or caregiver confirmed able to perform clean intermittent self-catheterization before randomization.

reports.label: Six-month randomized comparison
reports.citation: Visco AG, Brubaker L, Richter HE, et al. "Anticholinergic Therapy vs. OnabotulinumtoxinA for Urgency Urinary Incontinence." *N Engl J Med.* 2012;367(19):1803-1813. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1208872
reports.followUp: Mean change over months 1 to 6 of the double-blind phase; off-treatment follow-up to month 12

results.measure: Adjusted mean reduction in urgency incontinence episodes per day averaged over months 1 to 6 (baseline mean 5.0 per day); 241 women analyzed
results.note: Powered to detect a difference of 0.8 episodes per day (SD 2.1, 80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05 with one interim look); the report gives P only for the between-group comparison. 9% of monthly diaries were missing.

results.measure: Complete resolution of urgency incontinence among women returning at least four follow-up diaries
results.note: Secondary outcome; the report treats all analyses other than the primary as descriptive, without multiplicity adjustment.

results.measure: Complete resolution of all incontinence among women returning at least four follow-up diaries
More than 75% reduction in urgency incontinence episodes among women returning at least four follow-up diaries
Change from baseline in Overactive Bladder Questionnaire Short Form symptom-severity score (0 to 100; higher is worse), adjusted mean months 1 to 6
Change from baseline in Overactive Bladder Questionnaire Short Form quality-of-life score (0 to 100; higher is better), adjusted mean months 1 to 6

results.endpoint: Adequate symptom control after treatment ended
results.measure: Adequate symptom control (Patient Global Symptom Control 4 or 5 without off-study treatment) one month after oral study drugs stopped, month 7
results.locator: PMC3543828 Results, Follow-up after cessation of treatment; Figure 3
results.note: Percentage of the 121 toxin and 126 anticholinergic participants analyzed; 85/121 (70%) and 89/126 (71%) entered off-treatment follow-up at month 6.

results.endpoint: Adequate symptom control after treatment ended
results.measure: Adequate symptom control at month 12 (six months after oral study drugs stopped)
results.locator: PMC3543828 Results, Follow-up after cessation of treatment; Figure 3
results.note: The report prints P=0.61 for this comparison.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.note: Safety population (actual treatment received), P<0.001. Infection was a urine culture above 100,000 colony-forming units per milliliter or any antibiotic course for urinary infection.

harms.label: Intermittent catheterization by study criteria at 2 months
harms.note: P=0.01. By study criteria in the toxin arm only: 10/111 (9%) at 2 weeks, 3/112 (3%) at 1 month, 3/111 (3%) at 4 months and 1/106 (1%) at 6 months; the criteria were residual above 300 mL, or above 150 mL when rated moderately or quite bothersome.

harms.label: Self-catheterization since the previous visit at 1 month
harms.note: P<0.001. Includes catheterization outside the protocol criteria; at 2 months 14/119 (12%) versus 2/122 (2%), at 4 months 11/112 (10%) versus 1/121 (1%), at 6 months 5/111 (5%) versus 1/116 (1%).

harms.label: Residual volume above 150 mL at 2 weeks
Serious adverse events
harms.note: P=0.70; the investigators attributed none of the serious adverse events to study treatment.

delivery.label: Treatment regimen
delivery.value: Solifenacin 5 mg daily, raised to 10 mg at month 2 and switched to trospium XR 60 mg at month 4 when control was inadequate and side effects tolerable, plus a saline injection; or one 100 U intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA injection plus placebo pills escalated on the same schedule.

delivery.label: Catheterization rule
delivery.value: Intermittent catheterization for postvoid residual above 300 mL, or above 150 mL when the participant rated it moderately or quite bothersome.

delivery.label: Participants and baseline severity
delivery.value: 249 randomized (127 anticholinergic, 122 toxin), 247 treated (126 and 121), 241 in the primary analysis; baseline mean 5.0 urgency incontinence episodes per day and 41% anticholinergic-naive.
delivery.note: One toxin-assigned participant received active anticholinergic with placebo injection, as treated.

reports.label: Adherence analysis
reports.citation: Visco AG, Brubaker L, Jelovsek JE, et al. "Adherence to Oral Therapy for Urgency Urinary Incontinence: Results from the Anticholinergic Versus Botox Comparison (ABC) Trial." *Female Pelvic Med Reconstr Surg.* 2016;22(1):24-28. doi:10.1097/SPV.0000000000000215

results.measure: Overall composite adherence (mean percentage of expected doses from pill counts and electronic cap data), toxin arm taking placebo pills versus anticholinergic arm taking active pills
results.note: Planned secondary analysis. 53% of all women were at least 80% adherent in each of the three two-month periods.

reports.label: Trial-based cost-effectiveness
reports.citation: Visco AG, Zyczynski H, Brubaker L, et al. "Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Anticholinergics Versus Botox for Urgency Urinary Incontinence: Results From the Anticholinergic Versus Botox Comparison Randomized Trial." *Female Pelvic Med Reconstr Surg.* 2016;22(5):311-316. doi:10.1097/SPV.0000000000000277
reports.followUp: Six-month trial period; costs and symptom control modeled through 9 months

results.measure: Mean direct medical and nonmedical cost per participant over 6 months, 2012 US dollars, among 231 women completing 6 months (119 anticholinergic, 112 toxin)
results.note: Societal perspective by actual treatment received; indirect costs $106 versus $150 (P=0.62).

results.measure: Annualized quality-adjusted life-year gain from baseline (6-month utility gain times 2), derived from the OABq-SF
results.note: P compares the groups; both groups gained over baseline.

results.endpoint: Cost per month of adequate symptom control
results.measure: Modeled cumulative direct cost per month of adequate symptom control through 9 months (cumulative cost $1,266 toxin versus $1,942 anticholinergic)
results.note: Assumes no further toxin cost and sustained anticholinergic control after month 6; the oral drugs were actually stopped at 6 months in the trial.

relations.note: Both tested 100 U onabotulinumtoxinA in idiopathic overactive bladder with urgency incontinence; ABC used an anticholinergic comparator rather than placebo.
